title: Taxonomy enrichment and audit field proposals (Jun 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose and context:

This draft collects proposed enrichment fields, naming conventions, and a pragmatic versioning/migration approach for the audit event stream. It is meant to bridge a few current priorities: RBAC v2 rollout telemetry, evidence automation hooks for SIEM ingestion, and a minimal, backwards-compatible migration path across schema v1->v3 over the next two quarters.

Goals:
- Provide a small set of additive, well-documented fields that add signal for automated evidence linking and severity classification without breaking existing consumers.
- Define clear conventions for field names, typed values, and provenance so SIEM parsers and internal analytics can rely on them.
- Propose a staged versioning plan and migration checklist for customers and downstream systems.
- Surface RBAC v2-specific attributes we need to capture to validate policy decisions and to support forensics.

Design principles (short):
- Additive-first: new properties must be additive and optional; existing fields retained unchanged unless critical.
- Semantic stability: field names should be human-readable, consistent (snake_case), and self-documenting.
- Minimal cardinality: favor enums and short tags over free-text where possible to reduce SIEM index cardinality.
- Provenance and confidence: every derived/enriched field must include a provenance token and an optional confidence score.

Proposed enrichment fields (explanations and examples):
1) actor_disposition (enum)
   - Purpose: quick flag for actor identity confidence and type (service, user, proxy, unknown). Helpful for triage and automated blocking reactors.
   - Values: "human", "service", "api_key", "external_oidc", "unknown"
   - Example: "actor_disposition": "service"

2) actor_identity_origin (string)
   - Purpose: canonical origin token used to resolve where the actor assertion came from: "internal-iam", "oauth2", "saml-idp", "api-key-db".
   - Example: "actor_identity_origin": "internal-iam"

3) resource_ancestry (short list encoded)
   - Purpose: light-weight lineage for resources touched by an operation. Not a full tree—just up to 3 ancestry tokens. Reduces need for SIEM joins.
   - Encoding: comma-separated short ids (e.g., "proj:acme,env:prod,model:llama-65b")
   - Example: "resource_ancestry": "proj:acme,env:prod,model:llama-65b"

4) action_intent (enum)
   - Purpose: higher-level classification of an action vs. raw endpoint name. Useful for policy evaluation and alerting rules.
   - Values: "read", "mutate", "deploy", "rollback", "grant", "revoke", "admin"
   - Example: "action_intent": "deploy"

5) decision_context (string)
   - Purpose: short token capturing the policy engine decision set (e.g., "rbac-v2-cached-3m", "rbac-v2-decision-remote"). Helps replay and debugging.
   - Example: "decision_context": "rbac-v2-cached-3m"

6) policy_snapshot_id (string)
   - Purpose: immutable identifier for the policy state used at decision time (hash or tag). Enables deterministic audits.
   - Example: "policy_snapshot_id": "pshot-20260601-9f2b"

7) evidence_links (short list encoded)
   - Purpose: pointers (IDs) to binary or structured evidence (trail artifacts, request/response captures). Not full URLs by default; connectors expand them.
   - Encoding: pipe-separated ids, e.g., "ev:12345|ev:12346"

8) siem_index_hint (enum)
   - Purpose: allow producers to hint which SIEM index/category to route to: "alerts", "ingest_events", "forensics", "costing"
   - Example: "siem_index_hint": "forensics"

9) cache_state (enum)
   - Purpose: whether this event hit a caching layer that materially affects semantics (e.g., prefix cache, KV cache). Values: "miss", "hit", "stale", "partial"
   - Example: "cache_state": "hit"

10) severity_estimate (enum)
   - Purpose: lightweight estimated severity derived at ingest to improve triage and automated responder prioritization. Values: "low", "medium", "high", "critical"
   - Example: "severity_estimate": "medium"

11) ingestion_provenance (string)
   - Purpose: capture the producing pipeline identifier for downstream confidence and debugging (e.g., "producer:runtime-v2-az1").

12) model_artifact_fingerprint (string)
   - Purpose: for inference-related events, a short fingerprint of the model artifact used (deterministic hash/cc). Avoids leaking full artifact paths.
   - Example: "model_artifact_fingerprint": "mfp:8c3f2a"

13) tenant_exposure_flags (short bitset string)
   - Purpose: capture cross-tenant exposure signals (e.g., "none", "cross-tenant-read", "cross-tenant-write"). Keeps forensics aware of blast radius.

Versioning and migration plan (v1 -> v3):
- v1 baseline: current consumer set. No breaking changes. Production consumers expect existing keys (actor_id, resource_id, action, timestamp, request_id).
- v2 additions: introduce additive enrichment fields (actor_disposition, resource_ancestry, decision_context, policy_snapshot_id, evidence_links, cache_state). All optional. Provide schema registry entries for v2.
- v3 stabilization: standardize enum sets, publish full field docs, and enable parsers to surface severity_estimate and siem_index_hint. Keep all previous fields but deprecate ambiguous legacy fields (documented in mapping table).

Migration checklist (proposed rollout):
1) Week 0: Publish draft field definitions and enum lists (this doc).
2) Week 1-2: Feature-flagged producers emit v2 fields behind a toggle (no production consumers enabled).
3) Week 3-4: Internal SIEM parsers updated to accept and index v2 transiently; analytics teams test queries.
4) Week 5: Open beta to internal apps and solutions-eng; capture feedback.
5) Week 8: Announce deprecation windows for legacy fields (if needed) and publish full mapping guide.
6) Week 12+: Promote v3 stabilization and remove feature flags. Provide migration scripts/transforms for downstream systems.

RBAC v2 specific capture needs:
- capture role_source (string) to indicate whether role is inherited, assigned, or temporary
- capture grant_lifetime_seconds (int as string) for temporary grants (useful in incident triage)
- include decision_context and policy_snapshot_id (above) to reconstruct authorization outcome deterministically
- capture override_reason_id when a request was allowed by an escalation/override flow (ties into internal change control tickets)

SIEM export mapping notes:
- Avoid storing long arrays as separate fields (index explosion). Prefer short encoded strings and let connectors explode into parent-child relationships where necessary.
- Standardize timestamp format: RFC3339 with explicit timezone and millisecond precision. Field name: event_ts_rfc3339.
- Provide a static field 'schema_version' for each event with explicit semantic version (e.g., v2.0.0) to ease parser branching.
- Where possible mark high-cardinality fields as "non_indexed" in the central mapping to reduce index costs (example: model_artifact_fingerprint could be non-indexed and only used for lookups).

Evidence automation and forensics hooks:
- evidence_links should be resolvable by the evidence-service via short ids. The event should never embed binary data.
- Automatic enrichment pipeline should attach a 'collector_tag' that identifies which collector produced an evidence artifact.
- Define TTL policy for evidence artifacts and a retention token emitted in events (e.g., evidence_retention_days).

Open questions and trade-offs:
- How to represent multi-resource actions cleanly without explosion in cardinality? Proposal: limit resource_ancestry to 3 tokens and add a separate 'resource_count_hint' integer.
- Do we standardize a single severity algorithm or allow teams to emit their own severity_estimate? Recommendation: allow teams to emit, but add a platform normalizer that can annotate a platform_severity if desired.
- Backfill obligations for historical events: do we attempt to retro-enrich stored events? Recommendation: only enrich forward; provide lookup service for backfills on-demand.

Example pseudo-event (flat JSON line for SIEM):
{ "schema_version":"v2.0.0","event_type":"authz_evaluate","event_ts_rfc3339":"2026-06-12T16:42:03.123Z","request_id":"r:8af3-xyz","actor_id":"user:marc.chen","actor_disposition":"human","actor_identity_origin":"oauth2","action_intent":"deploy","resource_ancestry":"proj:acme,env:staging,model:alpaca-7b","policy_snapshot_id":"pshot-20260601-9f2b","decision_context":"rbac-v2-cached-3m","evidence_links":"ev:12455|ev:12456","siem_index_hint":"forensics","cache_state":"miss","severity_estimate":"low","ingestion_provenance":"producer:runtime-v2-az1","tenant_exposure_flags":"none" }

Next steps and immediate asks:
- Review enums and field names (security, SRE, solutions-eng). Flag objections or alternate vocab by EOD 2026-06-19.
- Engineering: implement producer feature flag to emit actor_disposition and decision_context in the runtime by 2026-06-26.
- Analytics/SIEM: prototype parser updates for v2 in a dev index and report indexing/cost implications by 2026-07-03.

Appendix: terminology and naming conventions (summary)
- Use snake_case for new fields.
- Prefer short token enums over free text.
- Always include schema_version and event_ts_rfc3339.
- When encoding small lists, use comma or pipe separators and document parsing rules per field.

References and pointers:
- CONFLUENCE-SEC/audit-taxonomy-landing (canonical landing page)
- JIRA-SEC-1427 (migration epic)
- github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1983 (producer change set)

Document history:
- 2026-06-05: Draft created by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-06-09: Added RBAC v2 capture notes (Marcus Chen).
- 2026-06-12: Incorporated SIEM parser feedback and proto example (Sofia Rinaldi).

----
Notes to reviewers: focus on the enum sets and cardinality concerns first. If you have an existing consumer that will break on additive optional fields, call out the consumer and sample events so we can surface compatibility mitigations.
